signals.title: JPY/SEK — G10 Bilateral Theme
signals.text: JPY leads the G10 currency strength scorecard with an average 1-week gain of +1.099% across 7 pairs, while SEK anchors the laggard rank at −0.607% across 2 pairs, producing a 1.706% bilateral spread. Japan July 2026 cash earnings surged +4.7% y/y against +3.9% expected, accelerating hawkish calls among BoJ board members ahead of the 18 Sep policy meeting. In contrast, Riksbank policy rates sit at 1.75% with persistent Swedish economic data misses reflected in an ESI of −26.7 against Japan's +21.8. JPY outperformance accelerates despite a nominal policy rate deficit of 75bp against SEK, indicating domestic monetary repricing is overpowering pure carry considerations. SEK vulnerability persists across European crosses as data underperformance compounds negative real rates. Trade bias: Bearish SEK/JPY, directional flow favoring yen monetary repricing. Catalyst: Japan Q2 GDP release today. Risk: BoJ leaves forward guidance unchanged at the 18 Sep meeting, triggering an unwind of recent hawkish pricing.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Crowded Positioning Squeeze
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 153.94, breaking cleanly below its SMA20 (158.72), SMA50 (160.33), and SMA200 (158.44) moving average cluster. The Saxo 25-delta risk reversal prints at −2.55, reflecting strong downside put skew and aggressive options demand for yen protection. Concurrently, CFTC Leveraged Funds hold net short JPY positions of −111,297 contracts, sitting in the 2nd percentile of their 52-week historical range at z = −2.18. This massive institutional short overhang leaves speculative accounts heavily exposed to rapid short covering as spot breaks technical supports. Realized 30-day volatility stands elevated at 11.3% against an implied volatility of 7.2%, creating a negative vol risk premium of −4.1% indicative of options pricing lagging rapid underlying spot moves. Trade bias: Bearish USD/JPY, speculative short squeeze forcing spot toward multi-month support. Catalyst: BoJ meeting 18 Sep — hike bias active. Risk: US August CPI beats on Friday, reviving the 268bp SOFR-TONA carry buffer.

signals.title: AUD/USD — Positioning + Retail Divergence
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.7225, holding comfortably above its SMA20 (0.7144), SMA50 (0.7048), and SMA200 (0.6992) stack. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold net long AUD positioning of +50,250 contracts, representing the 94th percentile of its 52-week range with z = +1.79, indicating crowded institutional exposure. Meanwhile, Myfxbook retail sentiment registers an extreme 90% short bias, directly opposing institutional futures positioning. Flow momentum shows institutional adds stalling with a weekly reduction of −3,328 contracts while the pair trades near cycle highs. While AONIA at 4.35% delivers a +69bp carry premium over SOFR at 3.66%, the combination of saturated speculative positioning and extreme retail short exposure signals late-trend extension vulnerability. Trade bias: Bullish AUD/USD, supported by carry but constrained by crowded positioning. Catalyst: China trade balance release today. Risk: China export data misses consensus, sparking an institutional liquidation toward the 0.7144 SMA20 anchor.

signals.title: GBP/USD — Elevated Vol Premium + Rate Parity
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3546, testing immediate resistance around its SMA20 at 1.3556 while remaining above its SMA50 at 1.3461. The CBOE 1-month implied volatility runs at 11.0% compared to a 30-day realized volatility of 4.5%, generating an elevated vol risk premium of +6.5%. Options markets are paying a steep premium for hedge protection into looming event risk despite a flat carry backdrop where the Fed policy rate at 3.75% matches the BoE at 3.75%. Leveraged speculative positioning sits in the 93rd percentile at +47,504 contracts long, though net exposure trimmed by −9,335 contracts WoW. The heavy options volatility premium indicates institutional hedging of sterling upside amid persistent policy uncertainty. Trade bias: Neutral/range GBP/USD, elevated options hedging capping near-term directional expansion. Catalyst: BoE Monetary Policy Report Hearings today at 13:15 UTC. Risk: BoE testimony delivers an unexpectedly hawkish policy path, resolving the volatility premium into an upside breakout above 1.3600.
